- **[Accepted Capability Set] a versioned SUT capability manifest, not a compile-time constant:** which Pulse P-IDs a scenario may name is **data** — `contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml`, read and bounds-checked at load (same `toml` + serde stack, no new dependency). Validation is two-layered: garde's `pid_format` asserts the `P-NNN` **shape** only, and `Scenario::check_capabilities` asserts **membership** against the manifest, applied by `Scenario::from_toml_str_with(&str, &CapabilityManifest)` at every load site that takes a `&CapabilityManifest` — the binary edges (`conductor-cli::paths`, `conductor-tauri::commands`) and the `conductor-core` catalog loaders that carry the manifest through (`list_scenarios(dir, &manifest)` for identity-only summaries, `load_catalog(dir, &manifest)` for the whole `Scenario` where a gate needs the phases a summary drops); the set is whatever takes that parameter, never a count. A malformed / absent / unparseable manifest is a **harness fault** (`CoreError`, `Result::Err`) carrying a named reason — never `Blocked` (a blocked row needs `run_id`/`seed`/`scenario`/`p_ids`/`slo_tier`, none of which exist at manifest-load time) and never a silent widening. The **accepted set** is data; the **coverage classification** stays code-native (`coverage_matrix()` in `conductor-core`, a no-runtime-IO `static`), and `check_sut_drift` asserts set-equality between the two — deliberately a two-source comparison, which sourcing the classification from the manifest would collapse into a self-check. So re-aiming at a newer Pulse release is a manifest edit **plus** a matching classification row: an accepted id with no row (or a classified id the manifest no longer accepts) is a `CoreError::SutDrift`, never a silent gap. **A second integrity gate sits beside it on a different axis:** `check_sut_drift` asks whether every accepted capability is *classified*, while `check_scenario_backing` asks whether every capability classified `Auto` — the mode that claims Conductor both drives the stimulus and asserts the reaction — actually has a scenario naming it. A capability can pass the first and fail the second, because classification is a statement of intent and a scenario is what makes it true. The `UNBACKED_AUTO` pin records the `Auto` claims no scenario yet backs, held to exact-set equality against the committed catalog (a new unbacked claim, a pin a scenario now covers, or a pin that lost its `Auto` classification are each a `CoreError::UnbackedCoverage`), so the ledger can only shrink under compulsion. Only `Auto` participates — `DriveObserve` is operator-confirmed by definition, and `StaticOnly` / `NotConductors` are deliberately not Conductor's to drive. `Scenario::from_toml_str(&str)` and `PId`'s shape are unchanged — garde's `dive` propagates `Context`, so threading the accepted set through garde would have forced a context onto `PId`/`PhaseSpec`/`EmissionSpec`/`ExpectedCheck` and changed `PId`'s public API.

- **[Module Boundaries] Crate-per-seam Cargo workspace:** In Rust, crates are compiler-enforced visibility boundaries; one workspace with a runtime-agnostic `conductor-core` plus the seam crates `conductor-timeline`/`conductor-emit`/`conductor-faults`/`conductor-verify`/`conductor-report` (+ `conductor-cli` bin and the `conductor-tauri` bin) makes a forbidden cross-seam dependency fail to compile, gives per-seam `cargo test -p` (and, with the qualifier below, `cargo build -p`), ships a single deployable, and mirrors Pulse's `crates/…` layout. The compiler enforces; cargo-modules/cargo-rail only audit. **The forbidden-edge property is compiler-enforced and unqualified; the standalone per-seam BUILD now holds for every member, measured rather than gate-enforced.** Workspace feature unification can mask a feature a crate uses but declares only in `[dev-dependencies]`, so a crate compiles in the workspace and in `cargo test -p` while failing alone. The standalone sweep takes the nine members each on its OWN targets — `--lib` for the seven library crates, `--bins` for `conductor-cli` and `conductor-tauri`, which have no lib target and would false-red under a uniform `--lib` — every one exit 0, measured twice (builder and operator). `--all-targets` is deliberately NOT the sweep form: it re-unifies dev-dependencies, which is the exact masking the sweep exists to catch. The caveat: no CI job builds a member standalone, so the property is measured-at-a-chunk rather than gate-enforced, and a future dev-only feature declaration could reintroduce it unnoticed.

- **[CI/CD] GitHub Actions, fmt + build + test + the static gates (over committed data · repository hygiene) + the Pulse-free a11y webview gate:** the `rust` job also carries a static gate per committed artifact that a production source derives — the `Coverage-completeness gate` (2026-09-06) and the `Scenario-assertion audit gate` (2026-09-16) — and two repository-hygiene gates (2026-09-24): the `Secret-scan gate` (no secret-shaped string or file name in `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`) and the `Workflow env-context gate` (every `env.X` expression read names a declared or `GITHUB_ENV`-written key, an admission a `GITHUB_ENV context probe` step pair re-measures each run). Each is its own named step with no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`, each opening its `run` with a presence guard on its subject that emits a `::error::` annotation and exits 1 so an absent subject fails loudly rather than passing vacuously, then invoking the specific nextest target (`-p conductor-report --test coverage_gate` · `-p conductor-core --test scenario_audit_gate` / `secret_scan_gate` / `workflow_env_gate`). Re-listing a gate's assertion in shell would be a second copy that drifts, so the gate IS the Rust test and the step is its presence-guarded invocation. The `rust` job opens with `cargo fmt --all --check` as its own named step (`Formatting gate (cargo fmt)`, step index 2, immediately after the toolchain install and before the cache restore, no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` — rustfmt is a `rust-toolchain.toml` component, so the gate adds no dependency and no lockfile delta; `--all` rather than the bare form because the workspace declares no `default-members`, making the two equivalent today and divergent the moment one is added); then `cargo build` / nextest / clippy on the dev OS target verify the harness compiles and unit/golden tests pass. The third job, `a11y` (`runs-on: windows-2022`), runs the routine webview a11y leg — `scripts/agent-run.ps1 run --e2e` under `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT`, invoked through the leg's entry point `scripts/a11y-token-witness.ps1` DIRECTLY, at the hosted step's native HIGH integrity, the asserting step carrying no `continue-on-error` and no `if:`; `scripts/a11y-limited-token-launch.ps1` survives only on the job's driver-alone diagnostics. Ahead of the routine arm, a `Pin msedgedriver to the image's WebView2 runtime (gate)` step reads the runtime from the two `EdgeUpdate` client keys, fetches msedgedriver for THAT version (§Occupied Resources — Ports), admits it through a pre-execution `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` gate (status `Valid` AND an `O=Microsoft Corporation` signer, non-zero exit on either arm), asserts driver major == runtime major and publishes `EDGEWEBDRIVER`, carrying no `continue-on-error` and no `if:` — then the reused `journal_conformance` gate over `runs/a11y`, then the violation-record artifact upload. The measured subject is driver/runtime COHERENCE, and the pin gate MAKES it rather than asserting it. It is a CI-time third-party binary dependency class that appears in no lockfile and that no lockfile-scanning gate covers (security-plan §Dependency Security), operator-ratified as a deliberate boundary widening. No runtime floor applies — a `≥ 152` floor is neither necessary (a coherent 131/131 pair runs the arm green) nor sufficient (a coherent 152/152 pair fails). What stays an operator/local gate is end-to-end dynamic scenario proof REQUIRING A LIVE PULSE (`mcp-server` feature + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`), because CI has no Pulse instance — not end-to-end per se: the routine a11y arm seeds its own committed fixture through the production writer and needs no Pulse, which is what makes it a CANDIDATE for gating — Pulse-freedom is NECESSARY, not sufficient, and hosted-runner runnability is a separate measured question (below). The driven (`a11y:driven`) and screen-reader (`sr*`) arms do need one and remain operator-local. Verdict: **the arm is GREEN in CI on the measured configuration — hosted `windows-2022` at a coherent 131.0.2903.86 msedgedriver + WebView2-runtime pair at High integrity, the driver pinned from the image's own runtime, 12 passing / 0 failing / 2 skipped, the `journal_conformance` gate run (`8 tests run: 8 passed`) and the violation record uploaded, as measured at run 35208593666 (headSha `fc4a9c2`, a11y job and whole run `success`)**. Every term in that sentence is load-bearing and the next image bump can move any of them, so it is stated with its configuration rather than as a bare verdict. Hosted-runner runnability is MEASURED and PROVEN for that configuration and unproven elsewhere. The leg also RUNS green on the Windows dev host through tauri-driver (0 failing, the expected-skip SET skipped), its hold-free Operable pair (SC 2.1.1 reachability · SC 2.4.3 focus order) environment-independent — measured green on two configurations differing in runtime major, driver major and coherence. The measured SET is now: hosted `windows-2025` at 152/153 — endpoint CLOSED at High; the Windows dev host elevated — CLOSED, non-elevated — OPEN; hosted `windows-2022` at a coherent 131.0.2903.86 pair — **OPEN at High**. Integrity's SIGN is therefore configuration-bound rather than universal: the Medium-integrity drop helped at runtime 153 on the dev host and BREAKS the session on `windows-2022` at 131, which is why the asserting step does not take it. **The MECHANISM — why an elevated token suppresses the endpoint THERE — is recorded, not established**: no probe measured it. Evidence: `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md`. The remainder is owned by the successor route entry, `v3-02` having returned to the pool.

A type-level verdict/error wall separates verification outcomes from harness failures: `enum Verdict { Pass, Fail, CalibrationRegion }` and `enum ReportState { Pass, Fail, ManualCheck, KnownResidual, Blocked }` are returned as `Ok(...)`; `Result::Err` means a harness fault (config parse, transport down, MCP unreachable). Read-back transport/decode/JSON-RPC errors fan out into `VerifyError` variants (`Transport`/`Protocol`/`Decode`/`JsonRpc` — blocked/fail/harness-error); garde's validation `Report` becomes a `ConfigError` harness-failure class via `#[from]`. `tonic::Status` codes and MCP error responses are first-class verification inputs, not panics.

When `ready` is false, every dependent auto scenario is emitted into the report with `state: "blocked"` and the named precondition — never pass/fail/manual-check. **The gate's named preconditions are FIVE:** protocol version-mismatch · required-tool absence · no incident opened after the canary storm was emitted (every incident in the corpus predates it, so Pulse raised none for this run) · **app/sidecar workspace-key agreement** · and **unmet run-contract terms** (`contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`, §Occupied Resources). **Which terms bind is POSTURE-selected (2026-09-22):** the gate evaluates under one L4 posture — `preflight_for(manifest, posture)` grades the contract through `RunContract::evaluate_for`, where a term tagged with a posture binds only under it and an untagged term under every posture. `conductor run` passes the scenario's declared `l4_posture`; `preflight()` delegates to the deterministic posture and remains what `conductor suite`, the GUI's run thread and `drive_run` call; `readiness()` (the `boot` verb) stays deterministic. A scenario whose declared posture differs from the posture its run's gate evaluated is recorded `Blocked` at SCENARIO level, before the ready check, with a message-borne log line naming both postures — never a sixth gate precondition. The last composes ONE string naming each unmet term individually — its condition and its candidate causes — and its arm sits after the tool checks but BEFORE the canary arms, because an unmet launch condition *explains* a failed canary: surfacing the canary symptom first sends the operator to the wrong cause, and with the contract's raised poll floor it would also spend the whole budget to do so.
